hypothesis: A cheap necessary physical cut-width resource can reject impossible simultaneous layer allocations during global pathing, before expensive local geometry and repair.
inequality: For a straight shared rectangular interface of length L, crossing centers may use both ends. At minimum copper width w and required gap c, at most K=1+floor((L+epsilon)/(w+c)) distinct electrical nets can cross on one layer. Ignoring obstacles, wider nominal copper, via occupation and corner inset makes this bound optimistic.
mechanism: Attach a shared resource descriptor to existing interface/layer ports only when K is smaller than the group's slot count, before and after duplicate-port generation. K>=slots is a nonbinding inequality because distinct owners cannot outnumber geometric slots; omit those descriptors entirely. A later enlarged group can become binding and is annotated on the second pass. Preserve every port and coordinate. Native candidate expansion permits a new owner only while fewer than K other net IDs occupy a binding resource. Same-net ownership at ANY other slot allows reuse. The native core, full/partial rerip and internal section evaluators inherit the reservation predicate. No slot sampling or density penalty is used.
ownership: Tiny portAssignment is NetId, indexed by mutuallyConnectedNetworkId; this never counts pair tasks as independent copper owners. Live assignment scans observe rip-up/backtracking immediately. Only immutable topology grouping is cached.
contracts: Exclude target/obstacle/off-board cells, fixed/preloaded/assigned interfaces, off-edge ports, and cells with any port outside their physical bounds. The theorem is a bound on the current port topology/interface contract, not a proof of global board infeasibility or sufficient routability.
physical_budgets: Use routing minimum width and the same minimum trace clearance selected by P9 joint DRC repair: srj.minTraceToPadEdgeClearance or RELAXED_DRC_OPTIONS.traceClearance. Native search, rip-up, HD, repair and quality budgets are unchanged.
hook_scope: One metadata-activated predicate wrapper under a coherent shared Symbol.for registry; original predicate, IDs, weak topology cache and weak problem references share that registry across module copies. Metadata-free inputs call the original predicate exactly once. P9 solver lifetime retains tracker strongly; detached descriptors fail explicitly.
timing: Annotation happens in the Tiny constructor outside the existing P9 phase timer. physicalCutSetupTimeMs exposes both annotation passes; end-to-end Blacksmith elapsed is primary. Live-owner predicate overhead is included in native work and measured by owner checks/assignment reads.
limitations: Native relaxed blocker discovery also sees binding resource reservations and may use its existing global rerip when it cannot identify a minimal cut-owner set. Removing a tautological descriptor also removes its old interference with relaxed blocker discovery at fully foreign-occupied interfaces; this follow-up therefore does not claim identical rerip trajectories to the original implementation. Binding-resource recovery and live scan overhead can still outweigh saved geometry. There is no occupancy cache, additional recovery policy or shortened budget.
validation: K=1 retains 2+ geometric slots and limits distinct simultaneous owners
Same-root tasks share the cut even when queried slot is free
Live capacity restoration after full reset and same-array partial backtracking
Core/selective/partial/full-section baseline and internal section-search predicate coverage
Physical annotation preserves every slot and protects fixed/off-edge contracts
K=1..4 and slot counts 1..6 retain only binding bounds, including K=slots-1; duplication activates a previously nonbinding inequality and contraction removes stale descriptors
Annotation plus native serialized loading and Tiny construction actually sends a second distinct root to another layer; original same-root allocation stays on layer zero
Unmodified e2e4 recognizes only nonbinding cuts and performs zero owner scans while preserving requested endpoints, internal continuity and independent copper DRC
Existing P9 differential-pair pad-clearance and Tiny regressions
positive_fixture: e2e4: 56 nonbinding-group observations over 2 annotation passes and 224 nonbinding-port observations; zero tagged groups, owner checks and assignment reads. All 28 unique eligible cuts have K>=slots. The annotated synthetic native allocation test supplies actual binding-resource activity and capacity rejections. This fixture's coverage is not a measurement of benchmark CPU savings.
followup_scope: The original source92018b7d annotated every eligible cut and its paired srj18 audit remains preserved separately. This follow-up only compiles away K>=slots inequalities, exposes physicalCutNonBindingGroups/Ports, and leaves K<slots live scans and native search/repair/physical budgets unchanged. Correctness-fixture zero scans do not establish weighted coverage or an end-to-end speedup; a new paired Blacksmith audit is required.
falsifiers: No meaningful cut saturation occurs on expensive benchmark cases
Predicate/live-owner or global-rerip overhead exceeds avoided work
Independent final quality or outcome regresses
Meaningful upstream resource activity still produces nowhere near a 10x end-to-end gain
performance_claim: None before paired Blacksmith results. Negative results apply to this optimistic per-interface width resource; they do not disprove general separator/cut certificates, coupled via resources or count-space routing.
